issues.quote: I looked at Rosa's kitchen clock when Madame's piano began.
issues.fact: The sheet says only "Rosa's clock" (L4 and L5), and gives no location for it. It is the same clock the master was holding in the kitchen that afternoon.
issues.misreading: "Kitchen clock" reads as a fixed fixture of the kitchen, so a solver could conclude the clock the master handled that afternoon was a different one. The 10:58 and 11:11 readings would then be attached to an untampered clock.

issues.quote: Each quarter is a doubled note, and the minutes past the quarter are high notes, quick and light.
issues.fact: The sheet says nothing about how the repeater sounds, only that it is a four-year project.
issues.misreading: The added description gives a sound-based method for reading the time, which a solver might apply to the clocks in the puzzle.

issues.quote: It is an old joke between him and the clock, and I do not think it has anything to do with this.
issues.fact: The sheet says only that the master said what he always says about the hall clock. It does not say the remark is a joke or irrelevant.
issues.misreading: The witness's dismissal tells the solver the hall-clock remark can be ignored, which the sheet does not support.

issues.quote: I was waiting for something, though I did not know what.
issues.fact: The sheet says nothing about the witness waiting for anything.
issues.misreading: It suggests the witness expected an event in the kitchen, adding a motive or timing hint not in the facts.

issues.fact: The sheet says only that the master made everyone show their watches at dinner.
issues.misreading: It suggests a fixed routine, implying the watch check was not a special or staged event.

issues.quote: and the master remarked on it.
issues.fact: The sheet says only that Girard would not take out his watch.
issues.misreading: It adds a remark by the master about Girard's watch, which is an extra fact about the master's attitude toward the watches.

issues.quote: I regulated it myself, so I knew it would be.
issues.fact: The sheet says only that her watch was exact.
issues.misreading: It adds a claim about how her watch was set and why she was sure of it.
